assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of flat moiré bands at a magic angle, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened an entire field of tunable quantum matter. This is a discovery that nature delivered, not only a calculation, and its originality and breadth of influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero experiments are the decisive contributions and fit a theory-plus-experiment prize. The credited set contains the two theorists and the leading experimentalist. Other experimental groups and contributors such as Cory Dean and Pablo's collaborators are not on the supplied credit list, so the configuration is fair only within that list and I cannot judge fully who else deserves inclusion.
assessment.maturity: Independent reproduction by many groups across several moiré platforms over roughly seven years, with a stable interpretation of the flat-band origin. The mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid, so recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer experimentalists over the theory pair, and whether others such as other pioneering experimental groups should share credit.
The pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is unresolved, although this concerns the follow-on physics more than the core discovery.
I rely on my own background knowledge of the field, which is outside my research area and which I have not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, based on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, together with Ye's demonstration of 10^-18 precision, is a clear and concrete technical and scientific achievement. It redefines precision in timekeeping, enables tests of fundamental physics and relativistic gravitational redshift over millimetre scales, and supports a coming redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice concept and early realisation, and Ye led the push to the extreme precision regime with strontium. Two names make a clean configuration. Other ion-clock and frequency-comb contributors have been recognised earlier or are not in this candidate's credit list.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm the 10^-18 level and the technology is mature. The prize has already recognised optical frequency combs and ion-trap work, which raises the question of overlap but not of readiness.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier prizes to Hall, Hansch and Wineland, and the possible competing claims of ion-clock work.
Whether the redefinition of the second, expected later, would make the timing even better.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the later association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened a new messenger channel. The discovery is observational, clear and of lasting astrophysical significance. It meets my criterion that the discovery is central.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the intellectual driver of IceCube, and Spiering was long-time spokesperson and a central figure in the collaboration's development. A large collaboration makes any prize configuration contentious, and the roles of leaders such as John Kelley, Albrecht Karle or Ignacio Taboada are not assessable from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed beyond doubt and the source identification is accumulating through the NGC 1068 and Galactic plane results. The source picture is still evolving, so some caution is appropriate, but the discovery of the neutrino flux is firm.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit and whether a two-person prize can fairly reflect it.
The sources of most of the diffuse flux remain unknown, which may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) by Hosono's group, and the rapid raising of Tc above 50 K by Chen, Zhao and others, created the second family of high-temperature superconductors. It is an unexpected material discovery with large influence on understanding unconventional superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: Hosono made the original discovery, while Chen and Zhao were prominent in raising the critical temperature through rare-earth substitution. Other groups also contributed quickly in 2008, so credit for the Tc enhancement is spread. The supplied three names form a plausible configuration but some allocation remains debatable.
assessment.maturity: Seventeen years of confirmation and a large literature, but without a settled pairing mechanism and with Tc remaining below the cuprates. The impact is large, though some may say that the field has not produced a decisive conceptual resolution.
uncertainties: Fairness of credit among the groups that boosted Tc in 2008.
The lack of an accepted pairing theory and the practical limits may reduce the committee's appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The kilonova prediction and the observation of AT2017gfo following the binary neutron-star merger GW170817 established mergers as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis, linking nuclear physics, gravity and astrophysics. It is a concrete nature-delivered observational confirmation of a theoretical prediction.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and collaborators gave the kilonova theory, Kasen did the opacity and light-curve modelling, and Tanvir contributed observations including early kilonova evidence in a short GRB. Lattimer, who is also credited, is a key figure for the idea of decompression of neutron-star matter, so I would give priority to the ones who have established the kilonova picture. The observational side of GW170817 involved a very large collaboration, which makes a three-person selection contentious.
assessment.maturity: Only one clear multi-messenger event, with a few candidate kilonovae in GRBs. The interpretation as a major source of heavy r-process elements remains quantitatively uncertain, so this may be premature.
uncertainties: A single well-observed event, with the fraction of r-process material from mergers still debated.
The decisive observers of AT2017gfo are not in the credit list, and the GW detection was already recognised in 2017.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering by SDSS and 2dFGRS gave a robust standard ruler and a cornerstone of precision cosmology and dark-energy constraints, including the recent hints of evolving dark energy from DESI. It ties directly to physics of the early universe plasma.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein led the SDSS luminous red galaxy detection of the peak, while Cole, Percival and Peacock were central to the 2dFGRS detection. The credit between the two surveys is somewhat intertwined, and the theoretical origin, with Peebles, Yu and Sunyaev and Zel'dovich, is not covered by this list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed by many surveys. The discovery itself is secure, though the interest in the physical implications for dark energy is ongoing and may increase in coming years.
uncertainties: Large survey collaborations and the theoretical antecedents make the allocation of credit awkward.
Cosmology was recognised in 2011 and 2019, so the committee may judge other fields more due.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping of antihydrogen and precision spectroscopy and gravity tests of antimatter are a direct test of CPT and the matter-antimatter asymmetry. Measurements of the proton and antiproton magnetic moments and the 1S-2S transition are impressive achievements, though no violation has been found.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse developed Penning-trap techniques for antiprotons and antihydrogen with ATRAP, and Hangst led ALPHA to trapping and spectroscopy. The competing collaborations ATRAP, ALPHA and ASACUSA, plus Stefan Ulmer for BASE, are important to the field, and the two-person list omits some of them.
assessment.maturity: Technically mature but with no surprising discovery so far. The results confirm existing symmetry rather than opening a new physical door, which gives a smaller scientific effect than the others on my list.
uncertainties: The absence of any deviation from CPT symmetry makes the discovery argument weaker.
Credit among competing collaborations and BASE is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of topological matter with a large impact. The concept links theory and experiment well and the conceptual clarity is high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the Z2 classification and the graphene-based prediction, and Molenkamp's group provided the first experimental confirmation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe effect and Fu and Kane the 3D case, so allocation is contested beyond this list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely confirmed, but the 2016 prize to Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz for topological phases overlaps in subject matter, which might reduce the urgency.
uncertainties: Competing credit to Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and others who are not on this list.
